Ollama Troubleshooting

Check /api/version and /api/tags on the same server address your client uses. A refused connection points to the address, port or server. If the version works, confirm the server has the exact model tag. For an HTTP 404, read the response body and check whether the client expects a native Ollama endpoint or an OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint.

  1. Check the exact server
  2. Connection refused
  3. Model not found or list is empty

Check the exact server

Run both calls from the same computer or network environment as your client. The example assumes a client and Ollama on the same machine with the standard port. Replace the origin if your client uses a different host or port.

curl --noproxy '*' -sS -i http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version
curl --noproxy '*' -sS -i http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags

A version response proves a server answered. In our two-server test, both returned the same version and only one had the model. Always check the model list on the same origin. For initial installation and a synthetic prompt, use the Ollama setup guide.

Connection refused

When curl reports error 7 or Connection refused, confirm the address and port. Open the Ollama app or start ollama serve if you use a CLI installation and no instance is already listening. Repeat the version request. A timeout is a different signal. Check reachability from the client before changing model or API settings.

If the client runs in Docker, its 127.0.0.1 points inside that container. Check the topology first and use the actual reachable service address. Docker Desktop provides host.docker.internal for reaching the host from a container. The host service must accept the connection at that address. The test below used two local processes and did not test Docker networking. See Docker Desktop networking.

Model not found or list is empty

Read models[].name in /api/tags and compare it with the client’s complete model ID. An empty list on a responding server can mean you reached another instance or a different model directory. Compare the origin and list first. Install the tag only if the intended server really lacks it.

If you created your own tag, check that ollama create completed on that server and use the output tag in the client. Verify a tag built with a Modelfile. For OpenCode, check its configured Ollama origin and model discovery.

HTTP 404 and the /v1 base URL

Choose the path based on the client’s API mode. The native API uses paths such as /api/tags or /api/chat. An OpenAI-compatible client typically takes http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 as its base and appends /models or /chat/completions.

In our run, putting a native path under /v1 returned a plain 404. Sending a missing tag to valid /api/chat also returned 404, with a JSON error naming the missing model. Check the response and endpoint together. If a client hides the response body, retry your specific method and path locally with curl -i. See the OpenAI-compatible endpoint examples.

After the API works

If a short request completes but normal prompts still fail, check the loaded context and processor with ollama ps. For a slow response or high memory use, try a smaller model or shorter context first and compare under the same conditions.

  • Check CPU and GPU placement
  • Estimate Mac memory before changing context
  • Unload an idle model and confirm it left memory

What we reproduced

One Apple M4 ran two isolated Ollama 0.40.18 instances. Both returned version 0.40.18. One listed the Qwen test tag, the other returned an empty list. We reproduced both 404s and stopped the empty instance to see curl error 7. The published responses omit unrelated fields.
